{{Short description|Annual award for film directing}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2026}} {{Infobox award | name = Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Theatrical Feature Film | image = Paul Thomas Anderson in 2025.jpg | caption = The 2025 recipient: [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] | awarded_for = Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Theatrical Feature Film | presenter = [[Directors Guild of America]] | country = [[United States]] | year = [[1st Directors Guild of America Awards|1948]] | holder = [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] for ''[[One Battle After Another]]'' ([[78th Directors Guild of America Awards|2025]]) }} The '''Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Theatrical Feature Film''' is one of the annual [[Directors Guild of America Awards]] presented by the [[Directors Guild of America]]. With 3 wins out of 13 nominations, [[Steven Spielberg]] is both the most awarded and most nominated director of this category in the history of DGA, and the first director to receive DGA nominations in six consecutive decades.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/11/movies/steven-spielberg-directors-guild-award-nominations-james-cameron.html |title=Steven Spielberg Gets a Record 13th Directors Guild Award Nomination |last=Buchanan |first=Kyle |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=January 11, 2023 |access-date=January 11, 2023 |url-access=subscription}} Additionally, [[Alejandro González Iñárritu|Alejandro G. Iñárritu]] is the only director to win twice successively; he was awarded in 2015 and 2016 for his directorial achievements for ''[[Birdman (film)|Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)]]'' and ''[[The Revenant (2015 film)|The Revenant]]'', respectively.{{cite web |url=https://slate.com/culture/2016/02/inarritus-dga-award-for-the-revenant-is-a-historic-win.html |title=Iñárritu's DGA Award for ''The Revenant'' is a Historic Win |last=Bastanmehr |first=Rod |work=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]] |date=February 7, 2016 |access-date=July 11, 2022}} Three directing teams have shared the award: [[Robert Wise]] and [[Jerome Robbins]] for ''[[West Side Story (1961 film)|West Side Story]]'' (1961), [[Coen brothers|Joel Coen and Ethan Coen]] for ''[[No Country for Old Men]]'' (2007), and [[Daniels (directors)|Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert]] for ''[[Everything Everywhere All at Once]]'' (2022). ==Predicting the Oscar's outcome== Since its inception the award has predicted the winner of the [[Academy Award for Best Director]] on all but eight occasions: * 1968 – [[Anthony Harvey]] (''[[The Lion in Winter (1968 film)|The Lion in Winter]]''); lost to [[Carol Reed]] (''[[Oliver! (film)|Oliver!]]''){{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/most-surprising-best-director-oscar-losers/ |title=10 Most Surprising Best Director Oscar Losers |last=McDade |first=Sean |work=[[Screen Rant]] |date=June 25, 2022 |access-date=July 11, 2022}} * 1972 – [[Francis Ford Coppola]] (''[[The Godfather]]''); lost to [[Bob Fosse]] (''[[Cabaret (1972 film)|Cabaret]]''){{cite web |url=https://collider.com/cabaret-bob-fosse-oscar-win-wasnt-upset-explained/ |title=Why Bob Fosse's Oscar Win for ''Cabaret'' Wasn't Just an Upset |last=Gaughan |first=Liam |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=March 6, 2022 |access-date=July 11, 2022}} * 1985 – [[Steven Spielberg]] (''[[The Color Purple (1985 film)|The Color Purple]]''); despite the film's 11 total Oscar nominations, Spielberg was not nominated for Best Director.{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-03-27-ca-1097-story.html |title=Academy Hits Racism Accusation |last=Friendly |first=David T. |author-link=David T.
